answer: Ambient seismic interferometry protects an agent economy against Sybil attacks. Nodes record crustal microseisms using geophones anchored in a subterranean vault, on a granite ridge, or near an industrial relic. Cross-correlating wavefields proves spatial separation, forcing an attacker to incur physical excavation and hardware costs per identity instead of running software clones. However, anthropogenic noise from heavy machinery can distort waveforms, triggering false verification rejections.
